samples.summary: New public `GridCanvas.linksInCell` (sref filter + dedup by URL) has no test; it is stubbed out everywhere it is used
samples.evidence: `linksInCell` is added in this diff and is what builds the hover card's URL list. gridcanvas-links.test.ts exercises `recordRenderedLink`, `linkAt` and `renderCellContent` but never `linksInCell` (no occurrence in the file). worksheet-links.test.ts supplies its own `linksInCell: (sref) => cells[sref] ?? []` in `hoverCtx` (line 57), so the real dedup/filter logic is mocked away. If the sref filter or the `seen` dedup broke, the card would list duplicate or another cell's destinations and nothing would fail.

samples.summary: Hover-card placement (flip/clamp), the 250ms close debounce, and the tab-switch reset in sheet-view.tsx are untested
samples.evidence: The diff adds a non-trivial useLayoutEffect computing left/top with flip-above and horizontal clamping, a 250ms `scheduleLinkHoverClose`/`cancelLinkHoverClose` pair, and `setLinkHover(null)` on engine teardown (whose comment explicitly describes a stale-card-on-tab-switch bug). The only new frontend test is SheetLinkPopover.test.tsx, which renders the card in isolation; there is no sheet-view test file (glob of packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/**/*.test.* shows only SheetLinkPopover, CommentPopover, image-*, csv-*). A regression here (card off-screen, card listing the previous tab's URLs) would ship silently, and frontend has no tsc lane either.

samples.summary: Wall-clock ratio assertions for linearity are nondeterministic and loosely bounded
samples.evidence: `expect(large).toBeLessThan(Math.max(small, 2) * 8)` and `... Math.max(fastest(plain), 2) * 20` compare timings taken inside the test process. The `Math.max(..., 2)` floor means the bound can be as loose as 16ms / 40ms absolute, so a sizeable constant-factor or mildly super-linear regression can slip through, while a loaded CI runner can make the ratio spike and flake the suite. These are presented as the guard for a performance property that has regressed twice per the comments; a deterministic operation-count or input-size-bounded assertion would actually pin it.

samples.summary: The `overlong` refusal (a URL run longer than MaxUrlLength links nothing) is not directly tested
samples.evidence: detectLinks refuses a span whose run exceeds MaxUrlLength (2048) — a deliberate 'never link a truncated destination' rule. cell-links.test.ts has no case with an otherwise-valid URL longer than 2048 characters; the only inputs that reach the branch are the adversarial perf shapes ('https://['.repeat(n)), which would return [] for unrelated reasons (unparseable authority). If the bound or the `overlong` comparison were wrong, a truncated URL could be linked and no test would notice.

samples.summary: The wiring that calls updateLinkHover from handleMouseMove, and resetLinkHover from the scroll handler, is untested
samples.evidence: updateLinkHover/resetLinkHover are tested in isolation in worksheet-links.test.ts by calling the prototype methods directly. The diff also adds the call sites: `this.updateLinkHover(e.offsetX, e.offsetY)` in handleMouseMove (before the cursor cascade) and `this.resetLinkHover()` in the scroll listener (packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts ~2804). worksheet-mouse.test.ts only asserts resetLinkHover on the drag branch and on mouseleave; no test drives the non-drag mousemove path or the scroll listener, so removing either call (leaving a card anchored to a scrolled-away cell) would not fail anything.

samples.evidence: The diff adds `if (this.pointerOverLink && scrollContainer.style.cursor === '') cursor = 'pointer'`. `pointerOverLink` is asserted in worksheet-links.test.ts, but nothing covers the cursor assignment or the 'only when nothing else claimed the cursor' condition.

samples.summary: The copy check-mark's 1500ms auto-revert is untested
samples.evidence: SheetLinkPopover.test.tsx asserts the check mark appears after a successful write and does not appear after a rejected one, but never advances timers to assert the `setTimeout(() => setCopied(null), 1500)` effect (or its cleanup on unmount).

The new exported helper has three branches; gridcanvas-links.test.ts covers left (implicitly, default align) and right ('places a span by the aligned line start'). No test exercises `align === 'center'`, where a mis-derived line start would misplace underlines, strikethroughs and link hit boxes alike.

samples.summary: `press()` swallows every rejection, so a throw inside the link branch would read as 'link not opened'
samples.evidence: `await handleMouseDown.call(ctx, e).catch(() => {})` deliberately ignores errors from the selection paths. The negative cases ('leaves a plain click to selection…', 'opens nothing where no span was painted', 'ignores a click on the headers') then assert only `expect(open).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`, which also holds if the handler threw before or inside the link branch for an unrelated reason. Narrowing the catch, or asserting the error is the expected downstream one, would keep these from passing for the wrong reason.

finding.summary: The rewritten cell-text paint path (per-span segmentation, link color, per-span underline, and the recording of hit boxes during render) has no test at all — only the two leaf helpers are driven directly
finding.evidence: The diff rewrites `renderCellText`'s inner loop: it now calls `detectLinks` per line, splits the line into segments, paints link segments in `linkColor`, draws per-span underlines only when `!style?.u`, and calls `recordRenderedLink` for each span. Nothing exercises this. `packages/sheets/test/view/gridcanvas-links.test.ts` calls `GridCanvas.prototype.recordRenderedLink` and `linkAt` on a hand-built `this` (lines 30-60) and never reaches `renderCellText`; `packages/sheets/test/view/gridcanvas.test.ts` covers only `computeCheckboxBox`, `buildRenderableRefs` and `renderCellCheckbox`. So if `renderCellText` stopped calling `detectLinks`/`recordRenderedLink`, computed the wrong `lineStartX`, double-painted glyphs, or drew two underlines, every suite stays green — yet hover, cursor and click all read that map, so the whole feature would silently not work. The repo already has precedent for testing a paint helper with a mock ctx (`renderCellCheckbox` + `makeMockCtx`, gridcanvas.test.ts:104-213), so this was reachable.
